sections.title: Section A: Multiple Choice (20 marks)
sections.note: Each question carries 2 marks. Choose the one best answer.

questions.text: A model scores 98% accuracy on a dataset where 98% of the samples belong to one class. What is the most sensible conclusion?
options: The model is excellent because accuracy is above 95%
Precision and recall must also be about 98%
The model may simply be predicting the majority class, so accuracy is misleading
The dataset needs no further checking

questions.text: In a fraud detection system, missing a real fraud is far more costly than raising a false alarm. Which metric should be given the most attention?
options: Precision
Recall
Accuracy
Specificity

questions.text: SMOTE is a technique that:
options: Creates new synthetic minority-class samples by interpolating between neighbouring minority samples
Copies existing minority-class samples exactly
Removes samples from the majority class
Scales all features to the range 0 to 1

questions.text: Feature scaling is most important for which of the following?
options: Decision trees
Random forests
Apriori algorithm
K-means and K-nearest neighbours

questions.text: A regression model has an R² of 0.85. This means:
options: 85% of the predictions are exactly correct
The model explains about 85% of the variance in the target variable
The average error is 0.85 units
The model is 85% accurate

questions.text: An association rule A → B has a confidence of 0.8 and a lift of 0.7. What does this tell you?
options: A and B are strongly positively associated
A and B always occur together
Having A makes B less likely than usual
Lift can never be below 1

questions.text: In K-means, what happens if K is set equal to the number of data points?
options: Inertia becomes zero but the clustering is useless
It gives the best possible clustering
Inertia becomes infinite
All the points merge into one cluster

questions.text: Which activation function is best suited to the output layer of a multi-class problem where each sample belongs to exactly one class?
options: ReLU
Sigmoid
Tanh
Softmax

questions.text: A 3 × 3 filter is applied to a 5 × 5 image with stride 1 and no padding. What is the size of the output feature map?
Which statement about parameter sharing in a CNN is correct?
options: Every position in the image has its own separate set of filter weights
The same filter weights are reused across all positions of the image
Pooling layers have trainable weights
Filters are designed by hand and are not learned

sections.title: Section B: Classical Machine Learning (24 marks)

questions.text: What is SMOTE and why is it used?
Why can accuracy be misleading on an imbalanced dataset? Name one better metric.
Why is feature scaling needed? Name two scaling methods.
Define precision and recall.
What is the F1-score and when is it preferred to accuracy?
State the difference between Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Mean Squared Error (MSE).
In the line y = mx + c, explain what m and c represent.
What does R² measure in a regression model?
What is a centroid in K-means, and how is each point assigned to a cluster?
What is the elbow method used for?
Define support and confidence in association rule mining.
What does a lift value greater than 1 tell you about a rule?

sections.title: Section C: Artificial Neural Networks (28 marks)

questions.text: What is a neuron (perceptron) in an ANN? State its three main parts.
What is the role of weights and bias in a neuron?
How is z (the weighted sum) calculated in a neuron? Find z for inputs x1 = 2 and x2 = 3, weights w1 = 0.5 and w2 = −1, and bias b = 1.
Why do we flatten an image before feeding it into an ANN (dense) layer, and what is the main drawback?
What is the importance of an activation function in a neural network?
Name four activation functions and state where each is commonly used.
State the purpose of the input layer, hidden layers and output layer.
What is forward propagation?
What is a loss function? Name three loss functions and state where each is used.
What do backpropagation and gradient descent do?
What is the purpose of an optimizer? Give three examples.
What is the learning rate, and what can go wrong if it is too large?
Differentiate between an epoch, a batch size and an iteration.
What is overfitting in a neural network? Name one way to reduce it.

sections.title: Section D: Convolutional Neural Networks (28 marks)

questions.text: What is a pixel? State the range of values in an 8-bit grayscale image and what 0 and 255 represent.
How is a black-and-white (grayscale) image represented differently from a colour image?
Name the three colour channels of an RGB image. What is the shape of a 28 × 28 grayscale image and of a 224 × 224 colour image?
What is a filter (kernel) in a CNN? Are the words "filter" and "kernel" the same?
What is a patch (receptive field) in a CNN?
What is a feature map?
Explain the concept behind stride, with an example. What is padding?
A 28 × 28 image is convolved with a 3 × 3 filter, stride 1, no padding. Show the formula and give the output size.

What is pooling and why is it used? Apply 2 × 2 max pooling with stride 2 to the matrix below.

1  3  2  1
4  6  5  2
3  2  1  0
1  2  4  8
What kinds of features do the early layers and the deeper layers of a CNN learn?
What is data augmentation? Give two examples and say why it is used.
What is the purpose of the flatten layer and the fully connected layer at the end of a CNN?
Give two reasons why a CNN is preferred to a plain ANN for image data.
A convolutional layer has 64 filters of size 3 × 3 and receives an RGB image. How many trainable parameters does it have, including biases? Show your working.
